reader.requirement: At 1985, for RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5 CHARACTERS the two integers only state the smallest and largest record sizes, and each record's size comes from its own record description entry (the integers do not bound or resize any record a WRITE sends or a READ delivers).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehaviors.IsActive(RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize, DialectLevel) sets VaryingRecordInfo.BoundsEnforced for format 3: false at 85, so VaryMin/VaryMax answer the record descriptions' own range; true from 2002 (GR19 there), so the integers bound WRITE/REWRITE

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the format 3 integers bound nothing (a 4-character and a 10-character record write with status 00 under RECORD CONTAINS 7 TO 8); at 2023 the same writes are unsuccessful with status 44 by that edition's GR19
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c23_record_format3_variable writes records whose sizes agree with integer-4 and integer-5; integers that disagree with the descriptions and an OCCURS DEPENDING ON record under format 3 are not in the witness

probes.printed: WA 00 WB 00 WC 00 / G 00 L=04 [ABCD] / G 00 L=04 [3xxx] / G 00 L=10 [9yyyyyyyyy] / G 10
probes.expected: sizes from the descriptions: R3A 4, the ODO record at its occurrences (II.2.1.4.2 for the implementor's variable choice, GR13 / DOC-A.1-148)

probes.printed: at --std 85: WA 00 WB 00 WC 00, records read back at 4, 4, 10; at --std 2023: WA 44 WB 44 WC 44
probes.expected: 1985 GR14: the size of each record is completely defined in its description, so integers 7 TO 8 bound nothing

probes.printed: RECORD CONTAINS 12 TO 4 compiles and runs at 85 with the same output as c5_rec3
probes.expected: 1985 states no syntax rule for format 3 (VII.3.8.3 has rules for formats 1 and 2 only), so nothing is refused

reader.notes: BindRecordClause keys format 3 by the absence of VARYING and records BoundsEnforced from the edition's DialectBehavior row; at 85 the connector's range is the descriptions' own, so the integers are documentation as GR14 says. The variable-length choice for format 3 is the documented implementor choice of GR13 (DOC-A.1-148).

refuter.evidence: The reader probed only a sequential file; I probed every organization GR14 reaches. r5_rec3_org3.cob (indexed DYNAMIC, relative DYNAMIC, each RECORD CONTAINS 7 TO 8 with a 4- and a 10-character record; sequential RECORD CONTAINS 2 TO 50 with a 10-character record; declaratives for the 1985 INVALID KEY / AT END syntax rules): --std 85 (runs/r5_rec3_org3-001) printed X1 00, X2 00, X3 00 [K02bbbbbbb], X4 00 [K01a], R1 00, R2 00, R3 00 [0123456789], R4 00 (REWRITE of the 4-character record over the 10), S1 00, S2 00 [0123456789], so the integers bound nothing and each record keeps its description's size; --std 2023 (runs/r5_rec3_org3-002) printed 44 on every indexed and relative write and S1/S2 00, the 2023 bound, showing the edition arm (BindRecordClause's RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize) is taken on every organization, not only sequential. Reading considered and set aside: GR15 defines a record's size with 'the maximum number of characters in any variable length item', which would make an ODO record's size its maximum, but GR15 itself adds 'This sum may be different from the actual size of the record', and II.2.1.4.2 lets the OCCURS DEPENDING phrase affect a variable length record's length, so the reader's ODO record written at its occurrences (GR13 implementor choice) stands. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR15'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13'; 'OK  §1985:II.2.1.4.2'.
